name: Prednisolone
summary: An intermediate-acting systemic glucocorticoid with potent anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive effects across many conditions.
mechanism: Agonist at the glucocorticoid receptor, modulating gene transcription to suppress inflammation, immune responses, and cytokine production.
pharmacodynamics: Broad anti-inflammatory, immunosuppressive, and metabolic effects; essentially no mineralocorticoid activity at usual doses.

dosing.adult: 5–60 mg/day depending on indication and disease activity; taper after prolonged use

safety.pregnancy: Use if clearly indicated; prednisolone is relatively favored among systemic corticosteroids in pregnancy
safety.lactation: Generally safe at low–moderate doses; high-dose courses warrant caution
contraindications: Live or attenuated vaccines while on immunosuppressive doses
warnings: HPA-axis suppression with >2–3 weeks of supraphysiologic dosing — taper, never stop abruptly
Infection risk and impaired wound healing
safety.overdose: Short-term excess: hypertension, hyperglycemia, psychiatric symptoms; supportive care, no antidote

indications: Rheumatoid arthritis and other autoimmune diseases
clinicalPearls: 5 mg prednisolone ≈ 20 mg hydrocortisone ≈ 0.75 mg dexamethasone — know your equivalence table.
Any course beyond 2–3 weeks requires a taper to avoid adrenal crisis.
good: Rapid, potent anti-inflammatory control across a huge range of conditions.
bad: Long-term use, active infection, uncontrolled diabetes, or osteoporosis.

provenance.notes: Curated from standard endocrinology/pharmacology references. Values omitted where not confidently known — nothing invented.
